conventions.convention: Hamiltonian fields satisfy ι_X_H ω = dH; the bracket is {F,G} = X_G(F) = −X_F(G).
A comoment map is real-linear with J([ξ,η]) = {J(ξ),J(η)}; its observable operator is ρ_J(ξ)F = {J(ξ),F}. No finite-dimensional or integration hypothesis is imposed on the real Lie algebra.
For left actions the fundamental field uses exp(−tξ), and moment components satisfy dμ^ξ = −ι_ξ_M ω. Consequently X_μ^ξ = −ξ_M.
The arbitrary-comoment assertion is choice-free. Only the moment-map branch assumes countable choice; equivariance implies the component bracket identity without connectedness of G.
The example uses real traceless matrices with commutator bracket, ω = dq ∧ dp, and J(H) = −qp, J(E) = q²/2, J(F) = −p²/2. Its coordinate-formula citation carries countable choice.

load_bearing.statement: For a real Lie algebra and a symplectic manifold, a comoment map is a real-linear map J into the smooth real functions satisfying J([ξ,η]) = {J(ξ),J(η)}. Define ρ_J(ξ)F = {J(ξ),F}. A Poisson derivation satisfies Leibniz rules for both multiplication and the Poisson bracket.

Every comoment map defines a real Lie-algebra representation on smooth functions by Poisson derivations, with ρ_J(ξ)F = −X_J(ξ)(F). Assuming countable choice, an equivariant moment map for a symplectic action of a finite-dimensional real Lie group supplies J(ξ) = μ^ξ and ρ_J(ξ)F = ξ_M(F), without requiring G connected.
